issue: When a defendant was sentenced under a mandatory guidelines scheme in violation of the Sixth Amendment, must the court grant full resentencing, or is a Crosby hearing (resentencing only if the judge would have imposed a materially different sentence) enough?

sides.position: A Sixth Amendment violation requires full resentencing, or at least remedies other than a Crosby remand are available.
A Crosby hearing is the appropriate remedy for a Sixth Amendment violation under a mandatory guidelines scheme.

quote: [T]he Supreme Court has not spoken to this issue, and there is a circuit split concerning whether violations of the Sixth Amendment require a full resentencing or a Crosby hearing.
cite: Ronald Morrell v. Warden, No. 20-1238 (6th Cir. 2021)
